name: element.list
title: List all elements
summary: Elements of a selection, sorted; optionally as derivation tree or in groups.

selection.description: Every part given must hold (SR-101 AK2).

sort.description: Keys in order: ties go to the next key, then to the workspace order (also without sort). `hierarchy` only first: the list is then the derivation tree, see `tree`. Without sort, the sort of the saved filter in `selection.filter`.

group.description: Group the list (SR-149): `type` (as written, a subtype is a group of its own), `status`, `package` (the property with the meaning `packages`), or the key of a property whose values element.facets offers: a choice or relation property, or a text, number or date property with few values shared in the workspace (a topic, not a title). Any other key is input.invalid. Groups come in the order a sort by the value gives: types, statuses and choices in metamodel order (a choice written by its display name is in the group of that choice), then other values: numbers, texts ignoring case, booleans; packages and other targets by title ignoring case, then short ID (spec-frage #978). Elements without a value form the last group; so do elements whose targets are all not available. An element with several values (packages, a list) is in each of their groups. `sort` (or the saved filter's sort) orders the elements inside each group; with `hierarchy` each group is its own tree. Nothing is stored.

withText.description: Also give the text of each element. Left out for an element without a version, and when its file changed while the list was built (list again).

elements.description: One page of the list. With `group`, the page of the grouped list (the elements of the first group, then of the next): an element in several groups is listed once in each, so a page can hold it more than once; key the rows by their position, not by the element.

tree.description: Only when `sort` starts with `hierarchy` (SR-075 AK2): the place in the derivation tree of each element of `elements`, in the same order. With `group`, each group is its own tree over its elements: a parent outside the group does not count. The list is the tree depth first: each root, then the elements below it. Each element of the selection appears once (spec-frage #354): below the parent of the list that reaches it at the shortest depth, the first in sort order among equals; an element without a parent in the list is a root, and so is the first element in sort order of a cycle that no root reaches. Its other parents are in its `relations`.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

depth.description: 0 for a root, 1 for an element below it, and so on.

parent.description: The element it is shown below, a parent of it by a derivation; left out for a root. It may lie on an earlier page.

groups.description: Only with `group`: every group of the whole list in order, also those on other pages; a group without elements is not given. `offset` and `rows` follow from the counts and are given for convenience.

value.description: Left out for the last group, the elements without a value. The type key, the status, the short ID of the package or target, the choice key, else the value as written. With a filter on it (`type` with subtypes false, `status`, `package`, a property condition with op eq) it selects the group's elements, except those that write a choice by its display name.

name.description: Display name of a type, status or choice of the metamodel.

title.description: Title of a package or target, when it has one.

identifier.description: Identifier of a package or target, when it has one.

unavailable.description: Only in the last group of a grouping by package or another relation property: its elements that name targets, none of them available (not on this machine or not in the workspace).

offset.description: Row of its first element in the grouped list: the group holds the rows offset to offset + count - 1.
Only with `group`: the row the page starts at (the `offset` of the input), so that a page can be headed by its groups without the input.

rows.description: Only with `group`: the rows of the grouped list, the sum of the counts of `groups`; `offset` and `limit` page over these rows. At least `total`, more when elements are in several groups.

total.description: Elements in the selection, each once.
